t.E517.agn: In 2019, EFSA re-evaluated sulphuric acid and its sodium, potassium, calcium and ammonium salts together; it decided that a numerical ADI was not necessary and that there was no safety concern at the reported use levels (in 1991 the SCF had set the group ADI as 'not specified'). A laxative (diarrhoea-inducing) effect has been reported in humans at sodium sulphate doses of 300 mg/kg body weight and above; the estimated intake from the food additive is far below this dose.
t.E517.body: Sulphate is absorbed from the digestive tract, distributes freely in the blood, does not accumulate in tissues and is excreted mostly via the kidneys; at high doses it is also excreted in faeces.
t.E517.eff.0.a: 300 mg of sodium sulphate or more per kilogram of body weight
t.E517.eff.0.t: A laxative (diarrhoea-inducing) effect has been reported; the estimated intake from the additive is far below this dose
t.E517.found.0: As a carrier in other food additives (quantum satis in the EU)
t.E517.prod: It is produced chemically by neutralising sulphuric acid with ammonium hydroxide.
t.E517.regx.0: Sulphuric acid and its sulphates (E 513–E 517) re-evaluated together; no safety concern, no numerical ADI needed.
t.E517.regx.1: Not included in Group I; permitted at quantum satis as a carrier in food additives (Annex III).
t.E517.summary: Ammonium sulphate. Used as a flour treatment agent that helps feed the yeast.
t.E517.what: It is an ammonium salt used as a carrier in other additives.
